ann_33.text: This part acts on 6 of 242 training patients (2%), patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy; 4 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 51-year-old woman classed as having no chest pain symptoms, with chest pain brought on by exercise, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it slightly lowers the predicted risk, from about 98% to about 97% (on the training data only; the model has little data on this).

ann_34.text: Through this part, a thallium result coded 4 raises the predicted risk, and even more so if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise: for a typical patient it goes from about 37% to about 88% with a flat ST segment, and from about 20% to about 31% otherwise. The model has little data on this: only 2 training patients (thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded)).
Only 2 training patients have a thallium result coded 4.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old woman classed as having no chest pain symptoms, with chest pain brought on by exercise, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), signs of left ventricular hypertrophy slightly lower the predicted risk, from above 99% to about 96% (on the training data only).
A flat ST segment and an abnormal thallium scan change that patient's predicted risk only slightly through this part (on the training data only).

ann_35.text: One small part barely changes the predictions.
Through it, chest pain on exercise and more ST depression on exercise raise the predicted risk only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_36.text: Through this part, typical angina (about 2%), non-anginal chest pain (about 3%) and atypical angina (about 9%) all clearly lower a typical patient's predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms (about 20%).
Being a woman lowers it through this part from about 20% to about 1% (on the training data only).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises it to about 88%, a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 42%, a flat ST segment to about 37%, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy to about 35%, higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) from about 12% to about 38% and more ST depression (0 to 2.8 mm) from about 15% to about 38% (on the training data only).
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 9%, and a maximum heart rate of 175 rather than 118 beats per minute from about 29% to about 15% (on the training data only).

For three rare categories the model has little data on this: a downsloping ST segment (17 patients; about 29%), a fixed defect on the thallium scan (15 patients; about 14%) and an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG (2 patients; slightly lower, about 16%), all on the training data only.
Older age (42 to 66 years) raises it only slightly, from about 17% to about 22% (on the training data only).

ann_37.text: This part acts on 29 of 242 training patients (12%), patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise and who have a flat ST segment; 24 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man classed as having no chest pain symptoms, with chest pain brought on by exercise, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it slightly raises the predicted risk, from about 78% to about 81% (on the training data only).
Through it, being a woman or having typical angina raises that patient's predicted risk from about 81% to above 99% (on the training data only).
Chest pain on exercise, a flat ST segment, an abnormal thallium scan and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy change it only slightly through this part (on the training data only).

ann_38.text: This part acts on 71 of 242 training patients (29%), patients with a flat ST segment; 40 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with non-anginal chest pain, no chest pain on exercise, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it raises the predicted risk from about 23% to about 56% (on the training data only).

Through it, having typical angina, atypical angina or non-anginal chest pain rather than no chest pain symptoms raises that patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 56% (on the training data only).
Chest pain brought on by exercise clearly raises it further through this part, from about 56% to about 70%.
Signs of left ventricular hypertrophy, sex and an abnormal thallium scan change it only slightly through this part (on the training data only).

ann_39.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with non-anginal chest pain (about 3%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 20%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises a typical patient's predicted risk to about 88%, a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 42%, and a flat ST segment at peak exercise to about 37% (on the training data only).

Higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) raises it from about 12% to about 38%, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) from about 15% to about 38%, and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG from about 20% to about 35% (on the training data only).
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 9%, and a maximum heart rate of 175 rather than 118 beats per minute from about 29% to about 15% (on the training data only).

For four rare categories the model has little data on this: a thallium result coded 4 (2 patients; about 31%), a downsloping ST segment (17 patients; about 29%), a fixed defect on the thallium scan (15 patients; about 14%) and an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG (2 patients; slightly lower, about 16%), all on the training data only.

Older age (42 to 66 years) raises it only slightly, from about 17% to about 22% (on the training data only), chest pain brought on by exercise changes it only slightly, and the model ignores resting blood pressure.

ann_33.original: The serial ReLU chain 2992 -> 4331 -> 3280 is a step function of restecg:2 (left ventricular hypertrophy): 3280 = 0.219*[restecg=2], exactly 0 otherwise. It feeds only the angina gate 665 (weight -0.951), contributing -0.208 there: an LVH inhibition term. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): Train scatter of 3280 vs restecg:2 takes exactly two values: 0 (restecg!=2, 123 rows) and 0.219 (restecg=2, 119 rows); correlation 1.0. Hidden chain values on restecg=2 rows: 2992=0.432, 4331=0.358, 3280=0.219.
ann_33.proposed: A part that acts on 6 patients with left ventricular hypertrophy and slightly lowers their predicted risk.

ann_34.original: Affine-in-practice context from restecg:2, thal:3, thal:4, slope:2. 2349 = 0.655 + 1.996[restecg=2] + 0.884[thal=3], clipped to 0 only for thal=4. 2771 = 0.938 - 0.573*slope:2 + 0.721*2349 (never clips). 2011 = 0.388*[thal=4] (a fixed-defect flag going to the output). 2349 and 2771 are inhibitory inputs to gate 665. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): On train 2349 takes only {0.655, 1.539, 2.651, 3.535} = 0.655 + 1.996[restecg=2] + 0.884[thal=3], and 0 on the 2 thal=4 rows. 2771 is active on 242/242 rows (range 0.31-4.01), so it is affine. 2011 is nonzero on exactly the 2 thal=4 rows (value 0.388); its logit contribution is 0.174 on those rows and removing it leaves train AUC unchanged (0.9528).
ann_34.proposed: A part through which a thallium result coded 4 (2 training patients) raises the predicted risk, more so with a flat ST segment; left ventricular hypertrophy slightly lowers it.

ann_35.original: 5884 = relu(-1.387 + 1.033*exang:1 + 0.075*oldpeak): zero without exercise angina; with angina about 0.075*(oldpeak_std + 0.75). Logit weight 0.211, so at most ~0.07 logit: an angina x ST-depression interaction that is nearly inert. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): 5884 is nonzero on 64/242 train rows, all with exang=1 (64 of 82 angina rows; 80% positive). Max value 0.346, logit term SD 0.013; ablating it changes train AUC 0.9528 -> 0.9526. Near-inert.
ann_35.proposed: A near-inert part: chest pain on exercise and ST depression raise the predicted risk only slightly through it.

ann_36.original: The 17 direct edges (via identity_0) are an exact linear logit (SD 3.46): male +2.99, asymptomatic cp:4 +2.06, ca +1.50/SD, cp:2 +1.21, thal:7 +1.06, fbs:1 -0.86, flat slope +0.86, LVH +0.80, chol +0.66/SD, cp:1 -0.63, oldpeak +0.54/SD; others < 0.5. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): Sensitivities equal |weights| exactly (linear). identity_0 has SD 3.46 vs total logit SD 3.81. Logit with only this term (+bias): train AUC 0.918, acc 0.831; full network AUC 0.953, acc 0.893.
ann_36.proposed: An additive part carrying most effects: any chest pain type, being a woman, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL and a higher maximum heart rate lower the predicted risk; more vessels, a reversible thallium defect, a flat ST segment, left ventricular hypertrophy, higher cholesterol and more ST depression raise it.

ann_37.original: Gate 665 is a thresholded vote. In indicator units its pre-activation is exactly -4.08 + 3.43[female] + 3.83[exercise angina] + 2.08[typical angina cp:1] + 0.46[flat slope] - 2.12[LVH restecg=2] - 0.85[normal thal=3] (the LVH and thal terms arrive through lvh_step and thal_lvh_context; thal=4 removes the thal/LVH inhibition). It is an exercise-angina gate: on train it fires on all 19 female+angina rows (mean height 1.78), on 14 of 59 male+angina rows only when slope is flat, there is no LVH and thal is abnormal (weak, mean 0.25; 12/14 positive), on 2/4 male+angina+typical-angina rows and 3/4 female+typical-angina rows; never without angina or typical angina (38/242 rows fire, 25 positive). It also passes the thal=4 flag 2011 from thal_lvh_context through to the output. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): Exact indicator-unit pre-activation (fit residual 7e-15 over all 64 combinations): -4.08 + 3.43[female] + 2.08[cp:1] + 3.83[exang] + 0.46[flat slope] - 2.12[restecg=2] - 0.85[thal=3]. Train firing: F+angina 19/19 (mean 1.78; 12 positive), M+angina 14/59 (all flat slope, no LVH, abnormal thal; mean 0.25; 12 positive), M+angina+cp1 2/4, F+cp1 no angina 3/4 (0 positive), all other 156 rows 0. Total 38 fire, 25 positive. Zeroing the gate (local copy): train AUC 0.953 -> 0.926.
ann_37.proposed: A part that acts on 29 patients with chest pain on exercise and a flat ST segment; through it, being a woman or having typical angina raises their already high predicted risk.

ann_38.original: Two serial ReLUs turn flat ST slope and the angina gate g=665 into a large risk term. In indicator units 3598 = relu(-2.298 + 3.098[flat slope] + 1.288 g) and 1650 = relu(-0.359 - 1.286[asymptomatic cp:4] + 1.944[thal=4] + 1.683*3598). So with flat slope, 1650 = relu(0.988 + 2.168 g) if chest pain is not asymptomatic and relu(-0.298 + 2.168 g) if it is: a flat-slope bonus of 0.99 (logit +1.42) that is withheld for asymptomatic patients (who already get +2.06 from the linear term), plus a slope-gated amplification of the gate (logit +3.1 per unit g). Without flat slope 3598 needs g > 1.78, so 1650 is almost always 0. The thal=4 flag 2011 passes through to the output. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): 1650 by (flat slope, asymptomatic cp:4, gate fires): (1,0,0) n=42 constant 0.990 (38% positive); (1,1,0) n=40 always 0 (80% positive, already high from linear cp:4 +2.06); (1,0,1) n=4 mean 2.57 (4/4 positive); (1,1,1) n=24 mean 2.71, max 7.59 (83% positive); no flat slope: 0 on 131/132 rows. Removing 1650 entirely: train AUC 0.953 -> 0.919, acc 0.893 -> 0.831; mean logit contribution on gate rows +2.84.
ann_38.proposed: A part that acts on patients with a flat ST segment and raises their predicted risk, more for patients with chest pain symptoms than without, and further if exercise brings on chest pain.

ann_39.original: Additive logit, then sigmoid: P(disease) = sigmoid(-1.018 + L + 1.430*A + 0.448*T + 0.211*E), where L = direct_linear_logit (identity_0), A = node 1650 from flat_slope_amplifier, T = thal=4 flag 2011 (0 or 0.388), E = angina_oldpeak_relu (5884). The network is a logistic regression over 17 inputs plus one sparse nonlinear correction (flat slope x non-asymptomatic bonus and the angina gate amplified by flat slope); T and E are near-inert. trestbps, fbs:0, restecg:0 and slope:1 have no edges and are zero-effect entries. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): Train: full AUC 0.9528 acc 0.893 logloss 0.282. Linear term only: AUC 0.918 acc 0.831. Without 1650: AUC 0.919. Without 2011: AUC unchanged. Without 5884: AUC 0.9526. Logit SDs: linear 3.46, 1.43*1650 1.80, 2011 term 0.016, 5884 term 0.013.
ann_39.proposed: Non-anginal chest pain lowers the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms. More vessels coloured, a reversible thallium defect, a flat ST segment, higher cholesterol, more ST depression and left ventricular hypertrophy raise it; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL and a higher maximum heart rate lower it. It ignores resting blood pressure.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk of heart disease about 20%), going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises the predicted risk to about 88% (on the training data only).

parts.original_hypothesis: Additive logit, then sigmoid: P(disease) = sigmoid(-1.018 + L + 1.430*A + 0.448*T + 0.211*E), where L = direct_linear_logit (identity_0), A = node 1650 from flat_slope_amplifier, T = thal=4 flag 2011 (0 or 0.388), E = angina_oldpeak_relu (5884). EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): Train: full AUC 0.9528 acc 0.893 logloss 0.282. Linear term only: AUC 0.918 acc 0.831. Without 1650: AUC 0.919. Without 2011: AUC unchanged. parts.name: flat_slope_amplifier
parts.original_hypothesis: Two serial ReLUs turn flat ST slope and the angina gate g=665 into a large risk term. In indicator units 3598 = relu(-2.298 + 3.098[flat slope] + 1.288 g) and 1650 = relu(-0.359 - 1.286[asymptomatic cp:4] + 1.944[thal=4] + 1.683*3598). So with flat slope, 1650 = relu(0.988 + 2.168 g) if chest pain is not asymptomatic and relu(-0.298 + 2.168 g) if it is: a flat-slope bonus of 0.99 (logit +1.42) that is withheld for asymptomatic patients (who already get +2.06 from the linear term), plus a slope-gated amplification of the gate (logit +3.1 per unit g). Without flat slope 3598 needs g > 1.78, so 1650 is almost always 0. The thal=4 flag 2011 passes through to the output. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): 1650 by (flat slope, asymptomatic cp:4, gate fires): (1,0,0) n=42 constant 0.990 (38% positive); (1,1,0) n=40 always 0 (80% positive, already high from linear cp:4 +2.06); (1,0,1) n=4 mean 2.57 (4/4 positive); (1,1,1) n=24 mean 2.71, max 7.59 (83% positive); no flat slope: 0 on 131/132 rows. Removing 1650 entirely: train AUC 0.953 -> 0.919, acc 0.893 -> 0.831; mean logit contribution on gate rows +2.84.

parts.name: angina_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Gate 665 is a thresholded vote. In indicator units its pre-activation is exactly -4.08 + 3.43[female] + 3.83[exercise angina] + 2.08[typical angina cp:1] + 0.46[flat slope] - 2.12[LVH restecg=2] - 0.85[normal thal=3] (the LVH and thal terms arrive through lvh_step and thal_lvh_context; thal=4 removes the thal/LVH inhibition). It is an exercise-angina gate: on train it fires on all 19 female+angina rows (mean height 1.78), on 14 of 59 male+angina rows only when slope is flat, there is no LVH and thal is abnormal (weak, mean 0.25; 12/14 positive), on 2/4 male+angina+typical-angina rows and 3/4 female+typical-angina rows; never without angina or typical angina (38/242 rows fire, 25 positive). It also passes the thal=4 flag 2011 from thal_lvh_context through to the output. parts.name: thal_lvh_context

parts.name: lvh_step
parts.original_hypothesis: The serial ReLU chain 2992 -> 4331 -> 3280 is a step function of restecg:2 (left ventricular hypertrophy): 3280 = 0.219*[restecg=2], exactly 0 otherwise.
